statement: Survey compiled 2026-08-29 compares sixteen archive/compression systems against specs and reference implementations; each substantive claim carries a URL; unverified cells left blank rather than guessed.
research_needed: Re-fetch sources before any superiority claim is published; versions and statuses date from 2026-08-29.

statement: Status counts disagree: header says 9 unverified cells, §12 heading says 10, and the matrices contain more *unverified* marks than either (WIM crypto, Apple remote/safe-extraction/unknown-feature, DwarFS unknown-feature, zpaq safe extraction, WIM bounds, zfec, Apple ECC).
research_needed: Re-count and reconcile unverified cells; publish per-cell status marks.
decision_needed: Which count and cell set is authoritative for the incumbent comparison ledger?

statement: Section 01 promises verified/conflict/unverified marks, but matrix cells do not carry per-cell verified marks, so the claimed 42 verified cells and 6 conflicts cannot be audited cell by cell.
research_needed: Annotate each matrix cell with status and source so counts are reproducible.

statement: RAR5 encryption is AES-256-CBC, not CTR: technote names no mode, UnRAR rijndael.cpp XORs plaintext with previous ciphertext block before encrypting; crypt5.cpp uses a non-null 16-byte per-file IV.
refines_or_supersedes: Corrects the stated premise supplied to the survey that RAR5 uses AES-CTR (§00 L11, §12 conflict 1 L377)
research_needed: Confirm aawc/unrar GitHub mirror matches current official UnRAR source.

statement: RAR5 has no MAC: integrity is mandatory CRC32 plus optional BLAKE2sp; flag 0x0002 makes checksums key-dependent to stop plaintext guessing, which is a privacy measure, not authentication.
RAR5 KDF is PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 with iteration count 2^Lg2Cnt, 16-byte salt and 16-byte IV per file; -hp encrypts headers following the encryption header.
WinZip AES uses PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA1 with 1000 iterations, AES-128/192/256 in CTR mode, and a per-entry HMAC-SHA1-80 (10-byte) tag computed after compression and encryption (encrypt-then-MAC).
WinZip AES carries a 2-byte password verification value, giving a 1-in-65,536 false accept of a wrong password.
decision_needed: How should a ZIP import adapter report a verifier pass followed by HMAC failure?

statement: WinZip AE-2 stores 0 in the CRC field; AE-1 keeps the real CRC as a redundant check.
research_needed: Corpus test that the ZIP import adapter handles AE-2 zero-CRC entries without false corruption diagnostics.

statement: In WinZip AES ZIPs, filenames, sizes and the central directory are never encrypted and the HMAC covers entry data only, never the central directory.
7z encryption is AES-256-CBC (CAesCbcEncoder/Decoder) with an iterated SHA-256 KDF over salt||password, 2^NumCyclesPower rounds, default power 19 (524,288), maximum 24.
research_needed: Verify against upstream 7-Zip source; cited file is from the mcmilk 7-Zip-zstd fork.

statement: 7z method registry names 7zAES as 06F10701 (AES-256 + SHA-256) and generic AES-256-CBC as 06F00181.
research_needed: Verify IDs against upstream 7-Zip DOC/Methods.txt.

statement: 7z has no MAC anywhere; only unkeyed CRC32s, which an attacker modifying ciphertext can recompute freely.

Survey rule: cells not established from a primary source are marked unverified and must not be filled in from memory or inference; implementation behaviour is stated where spec and implementation disagree.
Secondary documentation for archive formats is unusually stale; hosted 7-Zip method.htm omits LZMA2, ARM64/RISC-V filters and external codecs; source trees and release notes should be preferred.
Current 7-Zip(-zstd) codec registry assigns 0A to ARM64 filter, 0B to RISCV filter and 04F71101 to Zstd.
refines_or_supersedes: Source tree supersedes hosted help pages (§12 conflict 3 L379)
research_needed: Confirm whether 04F71101 (Zstd) is recognized by upstream 7-Zip or only the fork.
decision_needed: Should the 7z import adapter accept fork-only codec IDs such as Zstd 04F71101?

statement: The survey warns that hosted documentation.help 7-Zip pages are stale, yet cites that same page as the only source for the -mhe header-encryption switch and its default (off).
research_needed: Verify -mhe default and semantics against current 7-Zip source/help.

statement: Several 7z facts (AES, method IDs, codecs) are cited from the mcmilk 7-Zip-zstd fork rather than upstream 7-Zip; fork additions may not reflect the reference implementation.
research_needed: Cross-check each 7z cell against upstream 7-Zip source release 26.02.

statement: Codec scope determines almost everything downstream: whole-archive scope buys density and forfeits random access; per-entry scope buys random access and forfeits cross-file redundancy.
research_needed: Measure density vs random-access cost of Entrybound ChunkGroup scoping against whole-stream and per-entry baselines on shared corpora.
decision_needed: What codec scope granularity does the native format adopt by default in each profile?

statement: Per-inode (EROFS) and per-category (DwarFS) codec scope are the modern compromise between density and random access.
research_needed: Benchmark per-category scoping against Entrybound planner output.
decision_needed: Should the planner support per-category codec selection like DwarFS?

statement: ZIP codecs: Store, Deflate, Deflate64, bzip2, LZMA, PPMd, XZ, Zstandard (method 93, added in APPNOTE 6.3.7); codec chosen per entry.
research_needed: Measure which ZIP methods real-world readers (Windows Explorer, macOS, Info-ZIP, libarchive) accept, to set export target profiles.
decision_needed: Which ZIP methods may legacy export emit under each target profile?

statement: ZIP has no deduplication (identical files stored twice in full) and no dictionaries.
tar has no codecs in the container; gzip/zstd/xz/bzip2/lz4/lzop/lrzip wrap the whole stream; deduplication is hardlink entries only; dictionaries only via the outer codec.
7z codecs/filters: LZMA, LZMA2, PPMd, BZip2, Deflate, Delta, BCJ/BCJ2, ARM/ARM64/PPC/SPARC/IA64/RISCV; forks add Zstd/Brotli/LZ4/Lizard; codec scope is per folder.
research_needed: Determine which codecs/filters a 7z import adapter must support for realistic corpus coverage.
decision_needed: Which 7z coders are in scope for the import adapter, and what is refused?

statement: 7z solid folders give cross-file compression but not dedup; reaching one member costs full decode of the folder; no explicit dictionary object.
RAR5 has six methods (0 = store), compression algorithm version 0 (RAR 5.0+) and version 1 (RAR 7.0+); scope per file within a solid run sharing dictionary state (compression-info bit 6).
RAR5 dictionary size is 128 KB x 2^N, up to 64 GB in RAR 7.0, with non-power-of-2 sizes above 4 GB.
research_needed: Determine memory limits a RAR5 import adapter must enforce versus 64 GB declared dictionaries.
decision_needed: What dictionary-size ceiling should a RAR5 adapter refuse above?

statement: Zstandard: levels 1-19 and --ultra 20-22; whole-frame scope; no dedup, but --long extends window to 2 GiB and --patch-from deltas against a reference.
Zstandard dictionaries are first-class: --train, --train-cover, --train-fastcover, and a 0-4 byte Dictionary_ID travels in the frame header.
gzip supports only Deflate (CM=8); CM 0-7 are reserved and never allocated; raw deflate supports preset dictionaries but the gzip wrapper exposes none.
xz: LZMA2 (0x21) plus BCJ filters x86 0x04, PowerPC 0x05, ARM 0x07, ARM64 0x0A, RISC-V 0x0B; per-block filter chain; no dedup or dictionaries.
SquashFS codecs zlib, lz4, lzo, xz, zstd chosen for the whole image; compressed data blocks are checked for duplicates (block-level dedup), disabled by -no-duplicates.
EROFS codecs LZ4, MicroLZMA, DEFLATE, Zstandard chosen per inode; chunk-based dedup plus rolling-hash dedup of compressed data (-E dedupe); -E fragments merges file tails into a shared inode.
DwarFS codecs LZMA, Zstd, FLAC (audio), ricepp (FITS) plus null path for incompressible data, selected per category.
decision_needed: Should the Entrybound codec portfolio include domain codecs (audio, scientific) per category?

statement: DwarFS dedup has three layers: whole-file by XXH3-128; cross-file segmentation via cyclic hash (--window-size) with back-references across up to --max-lookback-blocks; nilsimsa similarity clustering places similar files adjacently.
research_needed: Head-to-head benchmark of Entrybound CDC+lookback+similarity clustering against mkdwarfs on identical corpora.

statement: Apple Archive codecs lzfse (default), lzma, lzraven, lz4, zlib, raw; per-archive block-based scope; dedup and dictionaries not documented.
zpaq ships the decompressor inside the archive as ZPAQL bytecode on a context-mixing model, allowing arbitrary codecs; the archived model is the dictionary mechanism.
zpaq uses content-defined chunking via rolling hash, about 64 KB average fragments, compared by SHA-1 across the whole archive history.
research_needed: Compare Entrybound CDC average size choice against zpaq ~64 KB and casync on dedup ratio and index overhead.

statement: WIM/ESD codecs XPRESS, LZX, LZMS; ESD is solid-mode LZMS; per resource or solid block; whole-file single-instancing by SHA-1 across every image in the archive.
Nix NAR has no in-format compression (compressed externally with xz/zstd in binary caches) and no dedup inside a NAR; dedup happens at store-path level.
OCI layers are tar, tar+gzip or tar+zstd with whole-layer scope; dedup is whole-layer by digest across images; no intra-layer dedup.
zstd:chunked dedups at chunk granularity using a per-layer manifest cache of full SHA-256 of each file and its chunks, then hardlinks or reflinks matches; eStargz uses gzip, SOCI unchanged gzip.
Comparison articles are most often wrong on encryption; the matrix distinguishes a real MAC from a checksum and reads every cell from a spec or source file.
APPNOTE defines ZIP signature records but they are effectively unimplemented; JAR signing is a META-INF convention layered on top, not a ZIP mechanism.
research_needed: Survey major ZIP implementations for signature-record (strong encryption/central directory signature) support.

statement: Legacy ZipCrypto is cryptographically broken and recoverable from known plaintext; it has no authentication and no name encryption.
research_needed: Cite primary cryptanalysis (Biham-Kocher known-plaintext attack) and measure prevalence in import corpora.
decision_needed: Should the ZIP import adapter accept ZipCrypto entries, and with what diagnostic/warning?

statement: tar has no encryption; encryption is always an outer layer (age, gpg, openssl) which also hides the member list, described as often the right architecture.
research_needed: Compare privacy and random-access cost of whole-stream outer encryption versus Entrybound encrypted metadata with indexed access.

statement: 7z encrypts archive headers (names/metadata) only with -mhe=on; the default is he=off.
research_needed: Verify default against current 7-Zip.

statement: Zstandard has no encryption or signature mechanism by design (RFC 8478), and the CLI has none.
gzip and xz have no encryption; xz offers only unkeyed integrity checks None/CRC32/CRC64/SHA-256.
SquashFS and EROFS have no in-format encryption; EROFS composes with fs-verity and dm-verity at the block layer, called a different and arguably better trust model.
evidence_in_source: opinion with primary citation for facts
research_needed: Security analysis comparing layered verity trust with in-format signatures for mounted archives.

statement: DwarFS documents no encryption in the format.
Apple AEA uses HKDF-SHA256, AES-CTR and HMAC with six named profiles covering signed-only, symmetric, symmetric+ECDSA, ECDHE-P256, ECDHE+ECDSA and scrypt password modes.
Apple AEA encrypts the whole archive stream including metadata, and HMAC is structural in every profile including the signed-but-unencrypted profile 0.
Apple AEA supports native ECDSA P-256 signatures (--sign-priv/--sign-pub) and is the only format in the survey with both native signing and native AEAD.
research_needed: Confirm no other surveyed incumbent offers in-format AEAD plus signatures before Entrybound claims parity/superiority.

statement: Characterizing AEA as native AEAD rests on an HKDF/AES-CTR/HMAC composition rather than a single AEAD primitive; key commitment and nonce-misuse properties are not addressed.
research_needed: Security comparison of AEA composition vs Entrybound AES-256-GCM-SIV plus HMAC commitment (commitment, misuse resistance, metadata coverage).

statement: zpaq uses AES-256 in CTR mode with scrypt KDF, encrypting the whole archive, with no authentication; its documentation says encryption gives privacy but not tamper protection.

WIM/ESD: some Microsoft ESDs are shipped partially encrypted in a form wimlib cannot decrypt (proprietary wrapper); whether names/metadata are encrypted and whether it is authenticated are unverified.
research_needed: Obtain [MS-WIM] spec and ESD encryption documentation.
decision_needed: Should a WIM adapter refuse encrypted ESDs outright?

statement: WIM has an optional integrity table of per-chunk SHA-1; signing is external via catalog files.

NAR and OCI have no in-format crypto and delegate to a digest-plus-signature layer above (Nix cache signatures; Notary/Sigstore/cosign), called the cleanest split: archive is a canonical byte string and signing is someone else's job.
research_needed: Evaluate whether Entrybound signatures over logical identity roots can also be exported to Sigstore/cosign-style external attestation.
decision_needed: Should Entrybound signatures be in-format, external, or both, and over which identity root?

statement: 7z, RAR5 and zpaq give confidentiality without integrity: a ciphertext-modification attack against any of them is not detected by the format.
research_needed: Demonstrate undetected ciphertext modification on each format as a reproducible test in the conformance/comparison corpus.

statement: Determinism and metadata fidelity pull against each other: recording more filesystem detail captures more environmental noise; NAR discards metadata, tar offers flattening flags.
research_needed: Measure identity stability of Entrybound LAI/PCR roots across hosts when full-fidelity metadata is captured versus normalized.
decision_needed: How does Entrybound separate identity-bearing metadata from environmental noise per identity profile?

statement: ZIP byte-identical output is achievable but not guaranteed: zip -X drops extra fields, TZ=UTC on extract, strip-nondeterminism normalizes Zip/Jar.
ZIP DOS timestamps have 2-second granularity and local-time semantics, itself a reproducibility hazard.
research_needed: Define LOSSY classification and timezone assumption for ZIP import/export of DOS times.
decision_needed: What timezone does ZIP import assume for DOS timestamps lacking extended time fields?

statement: Survey says ZIP mode/uid/gid are carried only via Info-ZIP Unix extra fields 0x7875 and 0x5455; ZIP has no standardized xattr or ACL storage.
research_needed: Verify against APPNOTE/Info-ZIP extrafld.txt: 0x5455 is the extended timestamp field and Unix mode normally rides in external file attributes, not an extra field.

statement: ZIP carries NTFS times via extra field 0x000A but no security descriptors or ADS; macOS resource forks travel out-of-band as AppleDouble under __MACOSX/.
research_needed: Corpus of macOS Finder-created ZIPs to test AppleDouble reconciliation in the ZIP adapter.
decision_needed: Should ZIP import fold __MACOSX AppleDouble entries into forks or keep them as plain entries?

statement: tar byte-identical output is best-in-class: GNU tar documents --sort=name --format=posix --clamp-mtime --mtime --numeric-owner --owner=0 --group=0, requiring tar >= 1.28.
PAX-header trap: GNU tar can embed timestamps and PIDs in pax header names/records, requiring a --pax-option incantation deleting atime/ctime and fixing exthdr.name.
research_needed: Verify exact conditions (POSIXLY_CORRECT vs --format=posix default exthdr.name with %p) under current GNU tar.

statement: pax extended headers give the highest POSIX fidelity in the survey: path, linkpath, size, uid/gid/uname/gname, atime/mtime with arbitrary sub-second precision.
Spec gap: xattrs and ACLs are not in POSIX pax; they ride on vendor keywords SCHILY.xattr.* and LIBARCHIVE.xattr.*, widely implemented but non-normative.
research_needed: Test matrix of which tar implementations read/write each vendor xattr/ACL keyword to set tar export target profiles.
decision_needed: Which vendor pax keywords does tar export emit, and which does import reconcile?

statement: Windows metadata in tar is carried only by pax vendor keywords; OCI defines Windows PAX extensions for file attributes, security descriptors, mount points and creation time.

7z reproducibility is unverified: no documented mode; timestamps stored by default and controlled by -mtc/-mtm/-mta; survey says treat as non-reproducible until proven, while §12 says absence is not proof and only forbids recording it reproducible.
research_needed: Empirically pack identical trees twice with 7-Zip 26.x across thread counts and compare bytes.

statement: 7z stores Windows-style attributes, with POSIX mode in the high bits of the attribute word by convention; security descriptors and ADS are not in the format; xattr/ACL coverage is unverified.
research_needed: Verify 7z xattr/ACL/ADS support in 7-Zip 26.x and p7zip forks.

statement: RAR5 determinism is unverified (none documented).
RAR5 stores UTF-8 names; non-representable Unix filenames are mapped into a private Unicode area with sentinel markers; max path length raised to 65,535 chars in 7.00.
research_needed: Adapter test for decoding RAR5 PUA-mapped names back to original bytes.
decision_needed: How should a RAR5 adapter reconcile PUA-mapped names into LogicalPath?

statement: RAR5 coverage of NTFS streams and security data, and 7z/RAR5 xattr/ACL/ADS coverage, are not established.
research_needed: Inspect RAR5 service headers (STM, ACL) in technote and 7z attribute handling.

statement: gzip is reproducible with -n/--no-name suppressing MTIME and FNAME; Reproducible Builds recommends gzip -6 -n; header MTIME, FNAME, OS byte and XFL are four independent nondeterminism sources.
decision_needed: What header values does compressed-stream export write for gzip (OS byte, MTIME, FNAME)?

statement: xz and zstd are deterministic given identical input and parameters including thread count; zstd --adapt output is not reproducible.
Survey says multi-threaded xz and zstd output differs from single-threaded output, so -T must be pinned.
research_needed: Measure whether output varies with worker count or only between single-thread and multi-thread modes in zstd 1.5.7 and xz 5.8.3; relevant to Entrybound thread-count-independent output.

statement: SquashFS explicitly supports reproducible images: -repro (equivalent to -mkfs-time inode), -repro-time sets both times, plus -force-uid, -force-gid, -all-root.
SquashFS has a full xattr table in the on-disk format, uid/gid via lookup table, hardlinks; Linux-oriented with no Windows ACL model.

EROFS explicitly supports reproducibility: -T sets a UNIX timestamp, --mkfs-time applies it to build time only, --all-time to every file; kernel doc frames images as bit-for-bit identical across deployments.
EROFS stores inline and shared xattrs and POSIX.1e ACLs via xattrs; EROFS_FEATURE_COMPAT_MTIME is a feature bit so per-file mtime is optional, described as a deliberate determinism affordance.
research_needed: Verify COMPAT_MTIME semantics in erofs_fs.h (compact vs extended inode mtime).
decision_needed: Should Entrybound make mtime an optional, identity-excluded field by default?

statement: DwarFS bit-identical images need --no-create-timestamp plus --no-history-timestamps or --no-history; --set-time flattens entry times; with --categorize --num-segmenter-workers must be held constant.
research_needed: Test that Entrybound pack output is byte-identical across worker counts, avoiding DwarFS's parallelism leak.

statement: DwarFS does not preserve extended attributes; it mounts on Windows via WinFsp but has no Windows metadata model.
research_needed: Recheck xattr support in DwarFS 0.15.6 before using in comparison claims.

statement: Apple Archive determinism is unverified: -include-field/-exclude-field gives a plausible mechanism (drop time fields) but no guarantee is documented.
research_needed: Empirical double-pack test with aa on macOS.

statement: Apple Archive has the highest macOS fidelity: ownership, permissions, flags, times, xattrs, error correction, APFS compression, full clones and sparse files; ACLs and BSD flags are first-class fields.
research_needed: Compare Entrybound macOS metadata namespace coverage field by field against Apple Archive.
decision_needed: Does Entrybound claim macOS fidelity parity with Apple Archive (clones, fs compression, BSD flags)?

statement: WIM/ESD determinism is unverified (none documented).
WIM has the best Windows fidelity: wimlib handles hard links, symlinks, junctions, named data streams and security descriptors; Linux capture maps to NTFS concepts.
research_needed: Compare Entrybound Windows metadata capture (SIDs, ADS, reparse points) against wimlib feature list.

statement: NAR is canonical by construction: directory entries ordered by name, strings length-prefixed (64-bit LE) and padded to 8 bytes.

NAR deliberately records only file type, contents, one executable bit, symlink target and directory structure; timestamps, ownership and general permissions are discarded, trading fidelity for canonicality.
decision_needed: Should Entrybound offer a NAR-like minimal identity profile excluding timestamps/ownership?

statement: OCI layer spec is largely silent on reproducibility; buildkit/docker buildx >= 0.10 honor SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH in practice.
OCI layers must carry mtime, uid, gid, mode, xattrs, symlink and hardlink references; sparse files SHOULD NOT be used due to inconsistent tar support.
decision_needed: When exporting to an OCI-layer target profile, must sparse files be densified?

statement: SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH normatively requires clamping, not setting: current-date timestamps use the value, and other execution-specific timestamps must be no later than it; GNU tar implements this with --clamp-mtime.
refines_or_supersedes: Normative SDE spec supersedes the Reproducible Builds docs page reading as 'set' (§12 conflict 5 L381)
decision_needed: Does Entrybound honor SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH, and does it clamp entry mtimes or only archive-level timestamps?

statement: Mounting an archive over HTTP range requests without downloading it is a different capability class, not an optimisation; this column separates 1990s formats from modern purpose-built ones.
research_needed: Measure Entrybound request count and latency for single-member remote reads versus zstd seekable, eStargz and ZIP EOCD strategies.

statement: ZIP: streaming create via data descriptors; streaming extract only partial because correct extraction needs the trailing central directory; random access via central directory and offsets; HTTP range works in practice (fetch EOCD then ranges) with no standard.
research_needed: Test ZIP import adapter behaviour when local headers disagree with central directory (stream vs index reads).
decision_needed: Does ZIP import trust the central directory or local headers when they disagree, and is disagreement REFUSED?

statement: Uncompressed tar is the archetypal streaming format with no index (O(n) scan), no remote access and no parallelism; .tar.gz adds pigz parallel compression but no random access or parallel decompression.
tar.zst has no random access unless built as a seekable frame set; zstd -T# is on by default up to 4 threads since 1.5.7; parallel decompression only across independent frames.
tar.xz supports per-block random access via the xz Index, but tar member offsets remain unknown without a separate index; multi-block enables parallel compress and decompress.
7z cannot be stream-created because the header is written last and can be relocated; solid folders must be decoded whole; random access is per folder; remote access poor.
decision_needed: Does 7z import require a seekable input (refuse pipes)?

statement: RAR5 stream create is limited; solid runs are sequential; a locator record can point at the recovery record and quick-open data.

Zstd seekable format places a seek table in a skippable frame (magic 0x184D2A5E) at the end; cumulative Compressed_Size gives each frame offset; frames are independent so random, remote and parallel access work.
decision_needed: Should Entrybound compressed-stream export optionally emit zstd seekable frames?

statement: SquashFS images are built offline and mounted; random access via block index, directory indexes and fragment tables; not natively remote; parallel compress/decompress per block.
EROFS is strictly block-aligned with prefix-binary-search directories; remote access via device table or over-network backends.
DwarFS benchmarks claim millisecond mount times and high-speed random reads via FUSE3/macFUSE/WinFsp; not natively remote.
research_needed: Independent measurement of open/first-read latency versus Entrybound INDEXED layout.

statement: Apple lists in-memory processing, streaming access and random access as Apple Archive API features, with multithreaded processing using all cores; HTTP range/remote access is unverified.
research_needed: Determine whether Apple Archive supports range-based remote reads.

statement: zpaq is an append-only journal with sequential extraction within a block, fragment-level random access via index, no remote access; ZPAQL runs at about half speed where not JIT-compiled.
WIM/ESD random access is per resource; solid ESD resources must be decoded as a unit; no remote access.
NAR has no index and no remote access, but the store-path layer above makes it unnecessary.
OCI layers have no random access or remote access; this gap is why eStargz/SOCI exist; gzip layers cannot parallel-decompress.
OCI row says zstd layers parallel-decompress 'yes', while the Zstd framed row limits parallel decompression to independent frames; a single-frame tar+zstd layer would not parallel-decompress.
research_needed: Check whether OCI zstd layers are typically multi-frame and whether decoders parallelize them.

statement: eStargz provides random and remote access via a JSON TOC (stargz.index.json) with per-entry offset/size; prioritized files placed first, separated by .prefetch.landmark, so a warm set arrives in one range request.
research_needed: Evaluate whether Entrybound STREAM/INDEXED layouts should support prioritized prefix ordering for warm-set fetch.
decision_needed: Should the planner accept an access-priority list that affects physical ordering?

statement: zstd:chunked keeps a TOC in a zstd skippable frame with per-chunk SHA-256 and offsets; chunks are compressed independently.
SOCI adds random and remote access to unmodified OCI layers via a separate index artifact stored with OCI Reference Types, so image digests and signatures stay valid.

SOCI's no-conversion property decouples the access index from artifact identity so adding seekability does not invalidate a signature; eStargz and zstd:chunked rewrite the layer and therefore change its digest.
research_needed: Decide and test whether Entrybound index/outboard structures fall inside or outside signed identity roots so re-indexing preserves signatures.
decision_needed: Is the Entrybound Index part of the signed identity, and can an index be added or rebuilt without re-signing?

statement: §05 asserts eStargz and zstd:chunked conversion changes the layer digest, but §12 item 10 says digest preservation is not addressed by their docs and the eStargz digest change was not confirmed.
research_needed: Convert a sample layer and compare digests and diff_ids.

statement: ZIP declares no memory, entry-count or expansion-ratio bound in the format, making it the zip-bomb substrate.
research_needed: Measure Entrybound declared budget enforcement against zip-bomb style inputs (overlapping, quoted, recursive).

statement: ZIP safe-extraction policy is not in the format; Info-ZIP unzip and other implementations each impose their own policy, inconsistently.
ZIP has no recoverability: central directory loss is often fatal and recovery tools scan for local headers.
decision_needed: Should Entrybound ZIP import offer a local-header scan salvage mode?

statement: ZIP fails open: 'version needed to extract' is advisory and widely ignored, there is no critical-feature bitmap, and unknown extra fields are skipped silently by design.
ZIP longevity: normative APPNOTE 6.3.10 (2022-11-01), many independent implementations, no official test vectors; Info-ZIP is effectively frozen (zip 3.00 2008-07-07, unzip 6.0 2009-04-29).
tar/pax format declares no resource bounds.

bsdtar safe extraction: strips leading slash from absolute paths, refuses paths with '..' components, and checks each extracted path for symlinks, replacing a final-element symlink with the archive entry; -P disables all three together.
research_needed: Compare Entrybound extraction confinement against bsdtar defenses, including intermediate-directory symlink races.

statement: bsdtar man page SECURITY section still advises inspecting with tar -tf first and not extracting as root.
decision_needed: Does Entrybound refuse or warn on privileged-restoration (ownership, setuid, devices) when run as root?

statement: Uncompressed tar degrades gracefully (damage costs affected members only); compressed tar does not, and a single corrupted byte typically destroys everything downstream.
research_needed: Corruption-injection experiment measuring blast radius of Entrybound chunk groups vs tar.gz/tar.zst.

statement: tar/pax fails open: POSIX reserves the all-lowercase keyword namespace but defines no must-understand marker, so unknown pax keywords are ignored.
decision_needed: How does tar import record unknown pax keywords (preserve as opaque metadata, drop with LOSSY, or refuse)?

statement: tar/pax has the strongest longevity: normative ISO/IEEE POSIX.1-2024 standard, many independent implementations, decades of interop.
7z coder properties declare dictionary size, which bounds decoder memory; there is no entry-count or ratio bound.
7-Zip safe extraction hardened reactively: 25.01 changed symlink handling with a -snld20 bypass; 26.01 added -spo output-path generation modes.
7z fails crudely: unknown codec IDs fail at decode, but no feature bitmap exists and unknown structural property IDs have no documented handling, so structural extensions cannot be safely rejected.
decision_needed: How should 7z import treat unknown property IDs: REFUSED or skipped with diagnostic?

statement: 7z has no normative spec (7zFormat.txt is a terse source note), LGPL reference implementation, current 26.02 (2026-06-25); no recoverability.
RAR5 technote permits refusing a KDF iteration count above a threshold, a rare explicit anti-DoS bound in an archive spec.
decision_needed: What maximum KDF cost (Argon2id parameters) will Entrybound readers refuse, and is it declared or reader-policy?

statement: RAR5 recovery is best in class: Reed-Solomon recovery records up to 1000% of protected data since 7.00, .rev recovery volumes up to 10x protected volumes, and a locator record to find the recovery record directly.

RAR5 explicitly mandates fail-open: unknown record types must be skipped without interrupting an operation, so a future interpretation-changing record makes older readers silently produce wrong output.
RAR5 is proprietary and single-vendor; UnRAR source is decompression only and its licence forbids reimplementing the compressor; WinRAR 7.23 release date unverified.
research_needed: Read the UnRAR license text directly to determine whether a clean-room Rust RAR5 decoder is legally permissible for an import adapter.
decision_needed: Is a RAR5 import adapter feasible under licensing constraints, and via clean-room or unrar binding?

statement: Zstandard declares required buffer size up front in Window_Descriptor (min 1 KB, max 3.75 TB); the RFC requires decoders to control memory and enforce system-specific limits; CLI defaults to a 128 MiB decompression limit.
decision_needed: What default decode memory ceiling does Entrybound enforce, and does it mirror zstd's 128 MiB?

statement: Zstandard integrity: optional XXH64 content checksum (low 4 bytes stored); independent frames localise damage.
Zstandard pairs fail-closed reserved bits (non-ambiguous error naming the unsupported parameter) with skippable frames as a fail-open metadata lane, called a genuinely good two-channel design.
decision_needed: Does ECF provide both a must-understand channel and a skippable ancillary channel for metadata/sections?

statement: Zstandard longevity is excellent (IETF RFC 8478, reference implementation, multiple independent decoders, 1.5.7 2025-02-19), but the seekable format is still v0.1.0 (2017-11-04) living in contrib/.
research_needed: Confirm current Zstandard RFC (RFC 8878 obsoletes RFC 8478) and whether cited requirements carried over; confirm latest zstd release as of audit date.
decision_needed: Is depending on the unstandardized zstd seekable format acceptable for any Entrybound export profile?

statement: gzip needs no resource bounds (fixed 32 KB window); CRC32 and ISIZE per member; multi-member streams localise damage somewhat; RFC 1952 longevity excellent.
gzip is fail-closed: a decompressor must error on any non-zero reserved bit since it could indicate a new field causing misinterpretation; called the clearest design rationale in any spec found.
xz filter properties declare dictionary size and xz enforces a memory limit, refusing inputs over it.
xz has per-block integrity checks (None/CRC32/CRC64/SHA-256) plus the Index, so a damaged block can be identified and skipped while the rest decodes: detection plus isolation, not ECC.

xz is fail-closed with reasoning: reserved bits must raise an error, and a CRC32 over Stream Flags lets old decoders distinguish corruption (CRC mismatch) from unsupported files (CRC matches but reserved bits set); unknown check types SHOULD warn or error.
decision_needed: Does the ECF preamble/feature field carry its own checksum so readers can distinguish corruption from unsupported features in diagnostics?

statement: xz spec v1.2.1 (2024-04-08); primary implementation XZ Utils 5.8.3 (2026-03-31); trust was seriously damaged by the 2024 backdoor.
SquashFS limits: max block 1 MiB, max file about 2 TiB, max filesystem 2^64 bytes; unsquashfs had write-outside-destination bugs fixed in 4.5.1.
SquashFS recoverability is described as none beyond per-block integrity, and unknown-feature handling as weak: a superblock flags field with no compat/incompat split.
research_needed: Verify whether SquashFS has any per-block checksum at all; the on-disk format is not known to carry one.

statement: SquashFS is in-kernel with squashfs-tools 4.7.5 (2026-03-01), documented in kernel docs rather than a standalone normative spec.

EROFS: block-aligned with bounded pcluster sizes; mounted read-only with user writes redirected to another trusted filesystem; optional superblock checksum; pairs with fs-verity for whole-image integrity.

EROFS uses a two-tier COMPAT/INCOMPAT feature design with a supported-mask; bits outside EROFS_ALL_FEATURE_INCOMPAT are incompatible, and the mask is derived so adding a feature extends the rejection set automatically; called the best unknown-feature design in the survey.
decision_needed: Should Entrybound readers derive their supported-feature mask rather than enumerate it?

statement: The survey calls two-tier EROFS the best unknown-feature design (§06) yet lists EROFS under 'three-tier feature bitmap' and calls the three-tier ext4 pattern strongest for mutation (§09); EROFS lacks a read-only-compatible tier.
decision_needed: Does ECF need a third read-only-compatible tier (readable but not safely repackable/appendable) in addition to compat/incompat?

statement: DwarFS: block size -S 20-26 bits; lookback blocks bound segmenter memory; mounted; no recovery; unknown-feature behaviour unverified.
research_needed: Establish DwarFS unknown-feature handling from source.

statement: DwarFS is single implementation, single maintainer, no normative spec; current 0.15.6 (2026-07-26) though the README still advertises 0.14.1.
refines_or_supersedes: Releases page supersedes README version (§12 conflict 2 L378)

statement: Apple Archive -block_size bounds the working set; safe extraction and unknown-feature behaviour are unverified.
Apple Archive lists error-correcting codes as a first-class archive field alongside digests and manifests, but the ECC algorithm is undocumented.
research_needed: Identify Apple Archive ECC algorithm from reverse engineering or clean-room implementations.

statement: Apple Archive longevity is the weakest: no published specification, single vendor, platform-locked (macOS 11+/iOS 14+), third-party support only via clean-room reimplementation.
decision_needed: Is an Apple Archive import adapter worth building given no published spec?

statement: zpaq ZPAQL VM is sandboxed with declared memory arrays, bounded by construction; safe extraction unverified; append-only journal keeps old versions and -until rolls back; no ECC.
zpaq has no unknown compression features because the decompressor travels with the data; level n implementations must read data from any level m with 1 <= m <= n.
zpaq is an open spec with reference decoder (Level 2 v2.06, 2016-03-22), effectively dormant since 2016; current maintenance status and later tool releases unverified.
evidence_in_source: primary citation for spec date only
research_needed: Check zpaq tool releases after 2016.

statement: WIM resource bounds, safe extraction and unknown-feature behaviour are unverified; [MS-WIM] spec exists but its version/date could not be retrieved (OpenSpecs URLs returned 404); all WIM claims derive from wimlib, which may differ from Microsoft.
research_needed: Retrieve [MS-WIM] and reconcile with wimlib behaviour.

statement: WIM has two substantial implementations: Microsoft and wimlib 1.14.5 (2026-01-29).
NAR needs no resource bounds (trivially simple grammar); Nix controls the target path entirely; no recovery.
NAR fails closed by omission: the grammar admits nothing unknown and has no extension point, deliberately.
NAR has a normative grammar and multiple implementations (Nix, Lix, Tvix, Go/Rust libraries); described as the simplest format in the survey and easiest to reimplement correctly.
research_needed: Compare line count/complexity of an independent minimal Entrybound reader against NAR readers.

statement: OCI whiteouts are the extraction hazard: .wh.<name> and .wh..wh..opq, and once a whiteout is applied the whiteout itself MUST be hidden.
decision_needed: How does an OCI layer import adapter represent whiteouts: as EntryKind, metadata, or REFUSED?

statement: OCI per-layer digest verification detects corruption but does not repair it.
OCI fails closed via media types: an unrecognised mediaType is not processable, so a new layer format cannot be misread; coarse (whole blob granularity) but costs only a registry.
decision_needed: Does Entrybound register a media type, and does a new major format version change it?

statement: OCI longevity is excellent: open spec, conformance suite, many independent implementations and an actual registry.
The highest-impact archive bugs of the last three years were name-resolution bugs (disagreements about which path an entry refers to), not memory-safety bugs.
research_needed: Systematic CVE classification across archive tools 2023-2026 to confirm the pattern.

statement: CVE-2025-8088: WinRAR <= 7.12 path traversal via crafted archive paths to arbitrary code execution (CVSS 3.1 8.8), exploited in the wild, CISA KEV.
research_needed: Add a conformance corpus case reproducing the traversal pattern for Entrybound import of RAR/ZIP.

statement: CVE-2023-38831: WinRAR < 6.23 parser differential; archive holds file x.jpg and directory x.jpg; UI resolves to the file, open path to the directory contents which execute; exploited in the wild, CISA KEV.
research_needed: Conformance corpus case: legacy archive with file/directory name collision must be REFUSED or reconciled deterministically.

statement: CVE-2025-11001: 7-Zip < 25.00 symbolic links inside ZIP files traverse to unintended directories, RCE in service-account context; fixed 25.00, hardened in 25.01 with -snld20 opt-out.
research_needed: Corpus case: symlink entry followed by entry writing through it must not escape the extraction root.

statement: CVE-2024-3094: deliberate Ed448-gated RCE backdoor in xz-utils 5.6.0/5.6.1 build, inserted by a maintainer after a multi-year social-engineering campaign; patched in 5.6.2.
Single-maintainer formats structurally carry supply-chain backdoor risk, which belongs in a longevity assessment.
research_needed: Audit Entrybound dependency tree (codec crates like xz/lzma bindings) for maintainer count and build-script risk.
decision_needed: Does the dependency policy exclude or sandbox single-maintainer codec dependencies?

statement: XZ Utils memory bugs: CVE-2026-34743 overflow in lzma_index_append() present since 5.0.0, fixed 5.8.3; CVE-2025-31115 multithreaded decoder flaw fixed 5.8.1.
research_needed: Confirm whether Entrybound's xz/LZMA codec dependency is a C binding affected by these or a pure-Rust implementation.

statement: libarchive advisories: GHSA-xgqq-r5j8-3mch ZIP writer heap OOB write with oversized pathname (2026-08-24, Low); GHSA-6vpf-5947-22g5 heap overflow in copy_from_lzss_window shared by RAR readers (2026-05-12, Low).
research_needed: Fuzz Entrybound legacy writers with oversized pathnames.

statement: Section 07 is titled as excluding ZIP, yet includes CVE-2025-11001 (symlinks inside ZIP files) and a libarchive ZIP-writer advisory; the ZIP CVE landscape itself is not covered in this appendix.
research_needed: Locate or compile the companion ZIP CVE survey and cross-reference it.

statement: WinRAR 7.13 fixed a directory traversal; 7.23 fixed a heap overflow in RAR5 recovery-volume reconstruction and a symlink extraction issue, showing the recovery feature is itself attack surface.

CVE-2023-38831 needed no memory bug or malformed data: a valid archive where two components disagreed about which entry a name denoted; formats permitting duplicate names or a name as both file and directory give this bug class for free.

Requiring a total order on names, forbidding duplicates, and forbidding a name from being both file and directory (as NAR ordered entries or a canonical-path-keyed manifest do) removes the parser-differential class structurally.
research_needed: Formal check that Entrybound LogicalPath invariants enforce all three properties and that no two code paths resolve names differently; extend to case-folding and Unicode-normalization collisions on target filesystems.
decision_needed: Does uniqueness also cover names that collide after case-folding or normalization on the extraction platform?

statement: Codec-level numbers are Silesia on one machine; whole-archive numbers are DwarFS's own vendor benchmark on datasets chosen to favour deduplication; ratios real but data highly redundant.
research_needed: Rerun on Entrybound's own corpus set with pinned tool versions, including low-redundancy data.

statement: lzbench setup: lzbench 2.0.1, Silesia corpus tarred, AMD EPYC 9554 single thread, GCC 14.2.0, Ubuntu 24.04.1.
Silesia: LZ4 reaches 47.60% of original at 577 MB/s compress and 3,716 MB/s decompress; LZ4HC -12 36.45% at 10.5/3,616 MB/s (memcpy baseline ~16,300 MB/s).

research_needed: Validate zstd level curve on Entrybound profile corpora to calibrate planner weights.

statement: zstd holds roughly a 10x decompression-speed advantage over LZMA across its ratio range, so paying for LZMA's ratio costs an order of magnitude on every read forever.
research_needed: Measure ratio gap and decode cost of zstd --long/dictionaries vs LZMA2/xz on Entrybound corpora, including multi-threaded decode.
decision_needed: Should LZMA-family codecs appear in the native codec portfolio at all, or only for maximum-density profile?

statement: Perl installations (47.49 GiB, 1.9M files): .tar.gz 12.17 GiB (3.90x, build 4m59s, open 2m07s); SquashFS 3.245 GiB (14.63x, 5m37s, 0.011s); 7-Zip 1.219 GiB (38.96x, 23m27s, 3.638s).
Perl dataset: DwarFS (zstd) 0.352 GiB (134.9x, build 5m03s, mount 0.009s); DwarFS (lzma) 0.310 GiB (153.2x, build 2m13s, mount 0.420s).
research_needed: Entrybound superiority claims on redundant corpora must be tested against these DwarFS figures on the same dataset.

statement: The DwarFS table shows the lzma build (2m13s) faster than the zstd build (5m03s), counter-intuitive for LZMA; likely differing options, hardware or versions not reported.
research_needed: Obtain exact mkdwarfs command lines and hardware for each row.

statement: DwarFS CI artifacts (465.2 GiB, 3.6M files): .tar.gz 142.9 GiB (3.255x, mount 22m18s); 7zip 60.04 GiB (7.748x, mount 10.5s); DwarFS zstd 28.63 GiB (16.25x, mount 0.024s).
Game audio assets (3.072 GiB, 171 files): .tar.gz 2.725 GiB (1.127x); 7zip 2.255 GiB (1.362x); SquashFS 2.711 GiB (1.133x); DwarFS 1.664 GiB (1.846x).
research_needed: Test whether Entrybound without a domain audio codec approaches DwarFS 1.85x on audio-heavy corpora.

statement: The ~150x figure is a deduplication result, not compression, and does not transfer to dissimilar corpora; dedup dominates codec choice when the corpus has repeated files and is irrelevant otherwise.
research_needed: Corpus stratified by redundancy to separate dedup gain from codec gain in Entrybound results.

statement: No incumbent versions (7-Zip, gzip, mksquashfs, DwarFS) or thread counts are stated for the whole-archive benchmark, so the figures cannot be reproduced or used as a fixed baseline.
research_needed: Reproduce with pinned versions before citing in superiority claims.

statement: Fail-closed unknown-feature mechanisms across file formats come in four structurally distinct shapes (per-element criticality bit, three-tier header bitmap, version gate with read/write split, reserved-must-be-zero bits); the choice between them is the design decision.
decision_needed: Which shape (or combination) does ECF use for unknown-feature handling, and is it documented against this taxonomy?

statement: Shape 1, a per-element criticality bit carried in each element's identifier, scales to unbounded extension vocabularies without any central registry of capability numbers.
decision_needed: Should ECF sections/metadata namespaces carry per-element criticality in addition to header feature bits?

statement: PNG chunk type bit 5 of byte 1 marks critical vs ancillary; decoders encountering unknown critical chunks must tell the user the image contains information it cannot safely interpret.
research_needed: Check PNG Third Edition (W3C 2025) for changes to chunk-property semantics.

statement: PNG adds a second axis most formats lack: a safe-to-copy bit telling editors whether an unknown chunk survives a rewrite; plus a private bit and a reserved bit that must be 0.
decision_needed: When Entrybound repacks an archive containing unknown non-critical sections/metadata, are they preserved, dropped, or refused, and is that declared per element?

statement: X.509/PKIX: a system MUST reject a certificate with an unrecognized or unprocessable critical extension; a non-critical extension MAY be ignored if unrecognized but MUST be processed if recognized.
OpenPGP: bit 7 of the signature subpacket type marks criticality; an unknown critical subpacket SHOULD make the signature be treated as in error; unknown non-critical subpackets SHOULD be ignored.
decision_needed: Must an Entrybound verifier reject a signature containing an unknown critical signed attribute?

statement: JOSE/JWS crit header lists header parameter names that must be understood; if any listed extension is not understood the JWS is invalid; the criticality marker is a separate index rather than a per-element bit.

Shape 2, a fixed three-tier feature bitmap split by what an ignorant implementation may still do, is the strongest pattern for anything with a mutation story because it separates 'read but not write' from 'do not touch'.
decision_needed: Does ECF feature tiering define a read-only-compatible tier governing append, recipient mutation and repack?

statement: ext4 superblock has s_feature_compat (0x5C, may read/write), s_feature_incompat (0x60, stop if unknown) and s_feature_ro_compat (0x64, may mount read-only); described as the canonical reference implementation of the pattern.
OpenZFS feature flags have three states (disabled/enabled/active) crossed with a READ-ONLY COMPATIBLE property; an active unsupported non-read-only-compatible feature blocks import entirely.
OpenZFS's enabled-but-not-active state lets a feature be switched on while old readers still work until it first changes the on-disk layout; once enabled, features cannot return to disabled.
decision_needed: Should ECF set a feature bit only when a feature is actually used in the archive (minimal-feature emission) so older readers open more archives?

statement: LUKS2 requirements array in JSON config is partially verified: functions exist in luks2.h, but normative spec text could not be retrieved (PDF returned binary), so exact semantics are unconfirmed.
research_needed: Retrieve LUKS2 on-disk format spec and document requirement semantics.

statement: SQLite uses write-version and read-version bytes (offsets 18, 19): read version 1-2 with write version > 2 forces read-only; read version > 2 means neither read nor write; user_version and application_id are informational only.
Two SQLite version bytes buy the whole ext4 tier structure: the cheapest version of the pattern that still works.
decision_needed: Is a read/write version pair sufficient for ECF versus a full feature bitmap?

statement: Shape 4, reserved bits that MUST be zero, is the weakest and most common form: it cannot express which feature is missing but prevents silently misparsing a stream when a new length field appears.
Zstandard decoders must produce a non-ambiguous error code and message explaining which parameter is unsupported; skippable frames 0x184D2A50-0x184D2A5F must simply be skipped and ignored.
decision_needed: Do Entrybound reason codes name the specific unsupported feature bit or codec rather than a generic unsupported error?

statement: For RAR5, if a future record changes how data should be interpreted, an older reader following the mandated skip rule silently produces wrong output.
decision_needed: Must a RAR5 import adapter REFUSE unknown record types despite the spec's skip mandate?

statement: ZIP ('version needed to extract' advisory, skippable extra fields), tar/pax (unknown keywords ignored) and 7z (no feature mechanism; unknown structural property IDs undefined) all fail open or undefined on unknown features.
research_needed: Per-adapter policy test: unknown extra fields/pax keywords/property IDs yield deterministic, reported outcomes in the observed-outcome matrix.
decision_needed: What is each import adapter's policy for unknown extensions (preserve opaque, drop LOSSY, or REFUSED)?

statement: Matroska/EBML must-understand marker is unverified: unknown elements are believed skipped using EBMLMaxIDLength (default 4) and size fields, not confirmed; survey says do not record it in a matrix.
research_needed: Check RFC 8794 (EBML) for unknown-element handling.

statement: zpaq eliminates the unknown-feature problem by shipping a sandboxed decompressor in the archive; the costs are that every decoder must implement a VM and the security surface becomes the sandbox.
decision_needed: Does Entrybound explicitly refuse embedded executable decoders (VM bytecode) as a design option?

statement: OCI media-type gating is coarse (granularity is the whole blob, not a feature) but genuinely fail-closed and costs nothing beyond a registry; described as worth stealing.
research_needed: IANA media-type registration process and timeline for the Entrybound container.

statement: EROFS incompat flag values appear duplicated in the extracted list (0x2 COMPR_CFGS/BIG_PCLUSTER, 0x8 DEVICE_TABLE/COMPR_HEAD2, 0x20 FRAGMENTS/DEDUPE), plausibly intentional reuse across contexts; erofs_fs.h must be re-read before recording bit numbers.
research_needed: Re-read erofs_fs.h directly.

statement: Formats separating logical content identity from physical bytes split into two families: canonical serialization that is hashed, and merkle structures over chunks letting physical storage vary freely.
decision_needed: Which family (or hybrid) do Entrybound identity roots LAI/PCR follow, and is this documented against this taxonomy?

statement: Nix store path digest is derived from the NAR hash (SHA-256 reduced to 160 bits, base-32); the fingerprint folds in type identifier, content hash, store location and name so changes to any are reflected.
research_needed: Verify whether the 160-bit reduction is truncation (as stated) or XOR-folding in the Nix implementation.

statement: Survey states that since a 2008 design change, SHA-256+NAR content-addressed data always uses the source: store-path construction regardless of how produced.
evidence_in_source: quoted primary citation; date attribution unclear
research_needed: Confirm the '2008' attribution against the Nix store-path documentation.

statement: Git object ID is the hash (SHA-1 or SHA-256) of '<type> <len>\0<content>'; storage as loose zlib objects or delta packfiles is unconstrained, so identity is independent of representation.

OCI images deliberately carry two identities: diff_id over the uncompressed tar and the manifest layer digest over the distributed blob; recompressing gzip to zstd changes the digest but preserves the diff_id.
OCI ChainID composes diff_ids in order to identify the result of stacking, binding layer order into identity.
decision_needed: How do Entrybound incremental base chains bind ordering into identity?

statement: OSTree checksums content/dirtree/dirmeta/commit objects individually and offers four storage modes (archive, bare, bare-user, bare-split-xattrs) for the same logical tree.
OSTree bare-user mode drops uid/gid and xattrs from the physical form while keeping the logical identity usable by an unprivileged process.
decision_needed: Can an unprivileged Entrybound extraction that cannot restore ownership still verify full logical identity and report FidelityReport differences?

statement: casync uses buzhash content-defined chunking, SHA512/256 (or SHA256) chunk digests, a small versionable .caidx/.caibx index, and a shared .castr store of individually compressed .cacnk chunks named by hash.
casync's last tagged release was July 2017; treat as a reference design rather than a production dependency.
composefs stores only the metadata tree in an EROFS image, optionally sealed with fs-verity, with file content in a separate content-addressed store referenced via trusted.overlay.redirect xattrs.
Because composefs generation is reproducible, the EROFS image digest is a stable whole-tree identity, and images share identical file content on disk and in page cache.

eStargz/zstd:chunked identity: TOC digest published as OCI annotation plus per-entry chunkDigest; verification is two-stage (TOC against manifest annotation, then each fetched chunk against its chunkDigest).
research_needed: Compare Entrybound partial verification of range-fetched chunks against this two-stage model.

statement: SOCI motivating data: image downloads account for 76% of container startup time, yet only 6.4% of downloaded data is initially needed.
PAR3 draft uses an InputSetID and per-packet Blake3 checksums, with chunk-based deduplication as a stated feature, unusual for an ECC format.

Every identity-separating system bought the ability to change physical encoding without changing identity (OCI recompress, Git repack, OSTree mode switch, Nix caches, SOCI index); formats hashing only physical bytes (ZIP, 7z, RAR) make recompression a breaking change and migration a re-sign event.
research_needed: Test that Entrybound repack with a different planner/codec preserves LAI and signatures while changing physical roots.
decision_needed: Which identity root do signatures bind by default so repack does not require re-signing?

statement: Design lesson: if an architecture will ever change codecs, define logical identity first and treat the container as a transport encoding.
Survey groups ZIP with formats hashing physical bytes, though ZIP CRC32 is computed over uncompressed data; the claim concerns signing/identity practice rather than per-entry checksums.
research_needed: Clarify which ZIP/7z/RAR integrity values are over logical vs physical bytes before using in superiority claims.

statement: RAR 5.0 recovery record can be as large as the archive; effectiveness depends on chosen size (commonly 1-10%); with multiple damage points even a maximum record may be insufficient.
research_needed: Quantify recovery probability vs parity overhead under burst and scattered damage models for external parity over Entrybound archives.

statement: PAR2 is Reed-Solomon over GF(2^16), the de facto standard for Usenet with a finalised 2.0 spec; par2cmdline v1.1.1 (2026-02-06) is OpenMP-threaded and actively maintained.
decision_needed: Is PAR2 the recommended external parity format for binding to Entrybound archives?

statement: PAR2 is external to the archive, which is its main advantage: it protects any file, including formats without a recovery story.
PAR3 is a stalled alpha draft (2022-01-28) awaiting a reference implementation; as of 2026-08-29 there is no finalised PAR3.
research_needed: Monitor PAR3 status before any binding design depends on it.

statement: PAR3 draft has pluggable codes (Cauchy matrices, sparse random matrices via PCG-XSL-RR, explicit LDPC/Tornado), any power-of-2^8 Galois field, any linear code; packets have magic, Blake3 checksum, length, InputSetID, type, and may appear in any order.

PAR3's feature ambition (empty dirs, UTF-8 names, UNIX/FAT/NTFS permissions, links, incremental backup, dedup, tail packing, large blocks, embeddable recovery) makes it effectively an archive format wearing an ECC format's clothes.

RaptorQ (RFC 6330, FEC Encoding ID 6) is a finalised systematic fountain code; decoding succeeds from almost any symbol set of sufficient cardinality; K'max 56,403 source symbols per block; symbol size 1-65,535 octets.
RaptorQ is designed for lossy network delivery, not storage, but its rateless property is attractive for archives where redundancy should be topped up later without regenerating.
research_needed: Assess patent/licensing status of RaptorQ and suitability for storage parity versus PAR2.
decision_needed: Should external parity binding support rateless codes for incremental redundancy top-up?

statement: zfec (Reed-Solomon erasure library underpinning Tahoe-LAFS): current version, parameters and maintenance state not verified.
research_needed: Investigate zfec status if considered for parity tooling.

statement: Apple Archive is the only mainstream archive format besides RAR with in-format ECC.
Per-block integrity checks plus an index (xz style) are the realistic middle ground for formats that do not want to carry parity.
research_needed: Validate Entrybound corruption localization granularity (per chunk/section) through fault injection.

statement: ZIP, 7z, tar.* and zstd have no recovery records, only detection (CRC32, XXH64, SHA-256 in xz).

Keeping parity outside the archive (PAR2) ages better than in-format parity (RAR): composes with any format, redundancy chosen after the fact, parity on different media, and ECC decoder kept out of the archive parser attack surface.
evidence_in_source: inference supported by WinRAR 7.23 recovery CVE
research_needed: Threat and usability study of external parity binding (sidecar discovery, binding to archive digest, repair workflow).

statement: If recovery is required, the strong default is a separate parity artifact over a canonical archive, not a format with parity baked in.
decision_needed: How is an external parity artifact bound to and discovered from an Entrybound archive (digest reference, filename convention)?

statement: WinRAR 7.23 release date is unverified; the vendor What's New page carries no dates.
Apple Archive ECC algorithm is undocumented; presence confirmed only.
zstd:chunked is not officially standardized or documented beyond comments and code in the reference implementation.

bsdtar --insecure: two man page renderings disagree whether it is a synonym for -p (preserve permissions) or -P (absolute paths); FreeBSD text groups it with -p; must verify against installed man page.
research_needed: Check libarchive source (bsdtar.c option table) for --insecure mapping.

research_needed: Close the two open conflicts before merging values into ledgers.

statement: All sources fetched 2026-08-29; spec and source-tree URLs preferred; no comparison articles used for encryption, determinism or capability claims.
research_needed: Re-fetch sources at release time; statuses (versions, CVEs, PAR3) will drift.

statement: Two claims rest on Wikipedia rather than primary sources: RAR5/UnRAR licensing (source 20) and the xz backdoor narrative (source 28).
research_needed: Replace with UnRAR license text and CVE-2024-3094 primary advisories.

statement: The survey cites RFC 8478 for Zstandard normative requirements and PNG 1.2 for chunk semantics; both have newer editions (RFC 8878; PNG Third Edition) not consulted.
research_needed: Re-verify quoted requirements against RFC 8878 and PNG Third Edition.

statement: Several matrix cells assert facts with no source link despite the stated method (ZipCrypto break, ZIP signature records unimplemented, 7z/ZIP/tar streaming and random-access cells).
